flows.title: How ambient access stops being invisible and becomes a type
flows.footnote: Verification re-runs the check against current source bytes. It never replays a stored answer.
flows.alt: Eight stages of the effect check: source, signature, checker, surface, profile, check, receipt, re-verify. A function that reads a file has to say so in its signature, and the checker follows effects through function values, closures, struct fields, control flow, and async blocks, so a callback cannot launder a capability. The whole set is the program's capability surface. A policy profile names what this build may reach, and the check compares one against the other before anything is built. The receipt seals the declared effects, the capabilities, and the source digests, and verification re-runs the check against the current bytes rather than replaying a stored answer. Two outcomes: passed, and rejected.

flows.kicker: one numeric run, sealed and re-checkable
flows.title: How a measured result carries the terms it was measured under
flows.footnote: A program that observes a model gets no receipt at all. Models propose, oracles dispose.
flows.alt: Eight stages of a scientific-runtime receipt: kernel, run, units, invariant, mode, seal, chain, re-derive. A numeric program's stdout is captured as a measurement series. A declared physical unit is canonicalized through a dependency-free dimensional-analysis core. One of eight invariants is checked over the series, each with a paired negative fixture that has to fail for the right reason. The mode records how the number was produced: deterministic, exact probabilistic, seeded stochastic, Monte Carlo with its estimator and interval, or budgeted search with its step ceiling. The seal carries the series, the claim, and the denominator. Any number of receipts chain into one ordered tamper-evident bundle, and verification re-runs the program rather than trusting the seal. Three outcomes: verified, failed, and refused.

cards.footnote: These rows are read from the same array buildc doctor prints, so the picture cannot outlive a re-ranked backend. Three of the nine reach the substrate receipt: c is recorded as the production anchor, rust carries an execution receipt over a corpus subset, and spirv is recorded as not yet runtime verified. The other six are ranked by what they emit, and nothing here records one of them running. A subset test passing does not make a backend production-ready.
cards.alt: A record card titled Every backend you can select, and how far each one goes, listing the nine buildc --target flags with the rank buildc doctor gives each one. The c row is accented as the only primary backend, the one the substrate receipt records as the production anchor. hlsl and glsl are supported shader source output, and the remaining six are experimental.
